discovery: Long-distance quantum communication: from fiber-based quantum key distribution and entanglement distribution to satellite-to-ground quantum networks

nominees.name: Jian-Wei Pan
nominees.affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei

nominees.name: Nicolas Gisin
nominees.affiliation: University of Geneva and Schaffhausen Institute of Technology, Switzerland

motivation: Gisin and Pan turned entanglement from a laboratory curiosity into a resource that can be distributed over global distances. Gisin pioneered practical quantum key distribution and long-distance entanglement over telecom fiber, including the first fiber Bell tests over tens of kilometers, quantum teleportation across fiber links, and quantum memories for repeaters. Pan developed multiphoton entanglement and teleportation techniques and led the Micius satellite programme, which achieved satellite-to-ground entanglement distribution over 1200 km, ground-to-satellite teleportation, and intercontinental quantum-secured communication, followed by a 4600 km integrated space-ground network. Together their work established the experimental foundations of the quantum internet, testing quantum nonlocality at unprecedented scales while showing that fragile quantum states can be engineered into robust, scalable technology. The 2022 prize honoured the foundational Bell tests; this nomination recognizes the distinct achievement of making entanglement-based communication work over real-world, planetary distances.
